key_insight: AI²-BPSP predicts the amorphous microstructure of poly(1,3-dioxolane) from first principles by simulating living polymerization and resolving chain-length-dependent diffraction signatures.
engineering_relevance: This enables atomistic, experimentally relevant design and validation of recyclable UHMW polymers whose disordered structures control mechanical performance.
method: Train reactive machine-learning force fields on van der Waals-corrected hybrid DFT data.
Simulate bottom-up living cationic ring-opening polymerization under experimental synthesis conditions.
Partition predicted X-ray and neutron diffraction into monomer and polymer contributions versus chain length.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports statistically significant, chain-length-resolved predictions of X-ray and neutron diffraction, including a monomer peak near q≈1.5 Å⁻¹ and a polymer peak near q≈1.6 Å⁻¹.
watch_item: The approach depends on force-field fidelity and simulated synthesis conditions, so transferability to other temperatures, initiators, or real experimental disorder may need validation.
paper_title: Bottom-Up Prediction of Amorphous Poly(1,3-dioxolane) using Ab Initio Reactive Machine-Learning Force Fields
